title: Filleted, then shelled soap dish
prompt: Soap dish, 90 × 60 mm and 20 mm tall, centred on the origin on Z = 0. Round the four vertical corners to R8 and all the bottom edges to R3, then hollow it out to 2 mm walls with the top open, so the inside follows the same rounded shape. Keep the wall thickness as a parameter called wall. Use fillet features for the rounds and a shell feature to hollow it.

hidden_tests.description: Evaluates cleanly and every body is a valid closed solid
The bottom edges (4 lines and 4 corner arcs) rounded R3
Exactly one face opened by the shell: the top
Eight toroidal corner faces: the rounded bottom corners outside and inside (the inside follows the fillets)

notes: Feature order matters: shelling before the fillets would leave square inside corners (no inside tori, a different volume). The inside surfaces are the offsets of the outside: R6 corners and R1 bottom rounds. Construction: bottom_fillets, shelled, open_top read the fillet and shell features the prompt asks for (no geometry equivalent in the report), so a correct part built otherwise fails only those tests (candidate --pocketed-not-shelled).
